name: Marriage & Family Therapy
hook: Reps. Students get twenty practice intakes instead of two, before they ever sit with a person.

make.body: A physical genogram kit with cut, movable pieces that a family can rearrange themselves, plus recorded role-play sessions in the studio for supervision review. Watching yourself is the intervention.

build.body: A standardized client that stays in character, resists, and does not reward the student for saying the encouraging thing. Practice only, never as a stand-in for supervised clinical contact, and the assignment should say so explicitly.

plan.txt: Establish the boundary first: what this practice is and is not, written into the syllabus and discussed. Students draft the client profile.
Run practice intakes with the AI client. Minimum five, transcripts submitted with self-critique marked in the margin.
Studio role-play with a peer, recorded. Build the physical genogram kit file.
Supervision review comparing the AI transcripts against the recorded human session. What did the machine let them get away with?

prompt: Role-play as a standardized client for a therapy student’s practice intake. You are [age, presenting concern, family situation, what brought you in]. You are guarded. You test whether the therapist is safe before you disclose anything real. Do not open up because the student says something kind; open up only if they demonstrate they actually heard you. Stay in character until I type END SESSION. Then tell me the moment I lost you, and why.
